request: Clarify the AI travel-agent context in the arXiv introduction and example, preserving the trusted payment service scope and results; do not publish.

changes.new_text:
Consider a travel business using AI agents to arrange a customer's flight and
hotel. A flight agent and a hotel agent submit payment requests to one trusted
merchant payment service, which controls payment credentials and authority.
Suppose the flight payment is confirmed, but the hotel payment has an uncertain
outcome. Stopping new requests leaves two questions: can the earlier hotel
request still execute, and do we know whether it has already done so? A booking
confirmation, a balanced reservation ledger, or a signed list of observed
payments does not by itself answer both.

We study one epoch on this merchant payment path. Agents propose requests;
the payment service, its journal, and the relevant source contracts are trusted.
Exact closure requires both a complete account of in-scope effect identities
and the exclusion of further effects under outstanding authority. The trust
boundary lies at the payment service: the agents cannot access its credentials
or internal state and need not trust each other's assertions. The travel setting
motivates the question; we do not verify composition across booking providers
or independent issuers.

The toy travel-agent scenario models requests to one trusted payment service.
Hotel capture requires an active flight. Its two failure modes were a commit-time
policy violation and an unusable trip; neither was a payment-completeness failure.
